I will keep the 7.8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation this year. That is what I know best, and around here in Quzhou most people with well water still do it this way. Cotton takes more watching, more picking, and more labor at the end, and my family has people working off-farm, so I will not put land into cotton this year. I usually start from what I did last year and only move a little. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the base fertilizer down before sowing, and then chase nitrogen once at jointing. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than see thin seedlings and low heads. With well irrigation, I will water wheat about 3 times if the year is normal: once after sowing or before winter if dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. For summer maize, I will follow right after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed, keep planting fast, and save labor with no-tillage. I will still feed maize enough because if maize is short and pale later, the yield loss is worse than the extra few bags of fertilizer money. I will spray each crop 2 times in a normal year, more only if insects or disease rise badly. My thinking is simple: first keep the land full, second keep water and fertilizer from falling short, third control costs enough so there is still money left for sprays and machine work.
